question: What did Urijah do when he heard that King Jehoiakim sought to put him to death?
choices: He was afraid, fled, and went into Egypt
explanation: When Urijah heard it, he was afraid, and fled, and went into Egypt.

question: What did Jehoiakim do with Urijah’s dead body after slaying him with the sword?
choices: Into the house of the king
Into the graves of the common people
explanation: Jehoiakim slew him with the sword, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people.

question: Where were all the people gathered against Jeremiah?
choices: In the house of the Lord
explanation: All the people were gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.

question: Where did the princes of Judah come up from when they heard these things?
explanation: When the princes of Judah heard these things, then they came up from the king’s house unto the house of the LORD.

question: Elnathan, who went to Egypt to fetch Urijah, was the son of whom?
explanation: Elnathan the son of Achbor.

question: Ahikam, whose hand was with Jeremiah, was the son of whom?
explanation: Ahikam the son of Shaphan.

question: In the days of which king did Micah the Morasthite prophesy?
explanation: Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah.

question: After Hezekiah feared the Lord and besought him, what did the Lord do?
choices: The Lord sent Micah to Babylon
The Lord repented of the evil he had pronounced
The Lord struck the king with sickness
The Lord gave Hezekiah a sign
explanation: Did he not fear the LORD, and besought the LORD, and the LORD repented him of the evil which he had pronounced against them?

question: The accusers said Jeremiah prophesied that the city would be what?
explanation: Why hast thou prophesied, saying, This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city shall be desolate without an inhabitant?

question: Who heard Urijah’s words with King Jehoiakim and all the princes?
explanation: When Jehoiakim the king, with all his mighty men, and all the princes, heard his words, the king sought to put him to death.

question: Whom was Jeremiah to speak to, standing in the court of the Lord’s house?
choices: The princes in the king’s house
All the cities of Judah that came to worship
explanation: Speak unto all the cities of Judah, which come to worship in the LORD’S house, all the words that I command thee.

question: What had the Lord set before them to walk in?
explanation: If ye will not hearken to me, to walk in my law, which I have set before you.

question: To whom did the priests and the prophets say, This man is worthy to die?
choices: The princes and all the people
The king and his mighty men
The elders of the land only
explanation: Then spake the priests and the prophets unto the princes and to all the people, saying, This man is worthy to die.

question: Against what did Jeremiah say the Lord had sent him to prophesy?
explanation: The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words that ye have heard.

question: The messengers who brought the yokes to Jerusalem came to which king of Judah?
explanation: Send them by the hand of the messengers which come to Jerusalem unto Zedekiah king of Judah.

question: By what does the Lord say he made the earth, the man and the beast?
choices: By the work of the prophets
By his great power and his outstretched arm
By the counsel of the nations
explanation: I have made the earth, the man and the beast that are upon the ground, by my great power and by my outstretched arm.

question: What do the prophets, diviners and dreamers keep telling the people?
choices: Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon
Ye shall be taken to Egypt
Ye shall be carried away for seventy years
Ye shall be made great kings
explanation: Hearken not to your prophets, which speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon.

question: What did Jeremiah tell Zedekiah to do?
choices: Make an alliance with Egypt and live
Hide in the mountains and live
Fight the king of Babylon and live
Bring your necks under Babylon’s yoke, and live
explanation: I spake also to Zedekiah king of Judah, saying, Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.

question: What will the Lord let the nations that serve Babylon do in their own land?
choices: They shall be carried to Babylon
They shall be given to Egypt
They shall till it and dwell therein
explanation: The nations that bring their neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, those will I let remain still in their own land; and they shall till it, and dwell therein.

question: Where will the vessels left in the Lord’s house be carried?
explanation: They shall be carried to Babylon, and there shall they be until the day that I visit them.

question: Jeremiah sent yokes to the kings of Edom and Moab and to which others?
choices: The kings of Ammon, Tyrus and Zidon
The kings of Egypt, Elam and the Medes
The kings of Philistia and Arabia
The kings of Uz and Dedan
explanation: Send them to the king of Edom, and to the king of Moab, and to the king of the Ammonites, and to the king of Tyrus, and to the king of Zidon.

question: Besides Nebuchadnezzar, whom shall all nations serve?
choices: His son, and his son’s son
explanation: All nations shall serve him, and his son, and his son’s son, until the very time of his land come.

question: When the time of Babylon’s land comes, who shall serve themselves of him?
explanation: Until the very time of his land come: and then many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him.

question: Why must the people not hearken to those who say, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon?
choices: They are paid by the king of Babylon
They prophesy a lie, to remove them far from their land
explanation: They prophesy a lie unto you, to remove you far from your land; and that I should drive you out, and ye should perish.

question: Besides the lands, what has the Lord given Nebuchadnezzar to serve him?
explanation: Now have I given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant; and the beasts of the field have I given him also to serve him.

question: What does the Lord say about the prophets who prophesy a lie in his name?
choices: He had sent them to Egypt
He had sent them in the night
He had sent them only to the priests
explanation: I have not sent them, saith the LORD, yet they prophesy a lie in my name.

question: Besides Zedekiah, to whom did Jeremiah speak, telling them not to hearken to their prophets?
choices: The priests and all this people
explanation: Also I spake to the priests and to all this people, saying, Hearken not to the words of your prophets.

question: Jeremiah asks: serve the king of Babylon and live; why should this city be what?
explanation: Serve the king of Babylon, and live: wherefore should this city be laid waste?

question: Whom did Nebuchadnezzar carry away to Babylon with Jeconiah?
choices: The nobles of Judah and Jerusalem
explanation: He carried away captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah from Jerusalem to Babylon, and all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.

question: How long shall the vessels remain in Babylon?
choices: Until the king of Babylon dies
Until the day that the Lord visits them
explanation: They shall be carried to Babylon, and there shall they be until the day that I visit them, saith the LORD.

question: What will the Lord do with the vessels when he visits them?
choices: He will melt them for the temple
He will give them to the nations
He will bring them up and restore them to this place
He will hide them in Egypt
explanation: Then will I bring them up, and restore them to this place.

question: What remained in Jerusalem when Nebuchadnezzar carried Jeconiah away, which the Lord says shall go to Babylon?
choices: The gold, the silver and the incense
The pillars, the sea, the bases and the vessels
The ark, the altar and the table
The harps, the trumpets and the cymbals
explanation: The pillars, and the sea, and the bases, and the residue of the vessels that remain in this city, which Nebuchadnezzar took not.

question: To whom does the Lord say he has given the earth?
choices: To whom it seemed meet to him
To the king of Babylon alone
explanation: I have given it unto whom it seemed meet unto me.

question: Whom did Jeremiah ask, Why will ye die, thou and thy people, by the sword, famine and pestilence?
explanation: Why will ye die, thou and thy people, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence?

question: Where were the remaining vessels that the true prophets could intercede for?
choices: In the cities of Edom and Moab
In the house of the prophets
The Lord’s house, the king’s house and Jerusalem
In the valley and the gate
explanation: The vessels which are left in the house of the LORD, and in the house of the king of Judah, and at Jerusalem.

question: Jeconiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away, was the son of which king?
explanation: Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah.

question: Which of these is listed with prophets, diviners, enchanters and sorcerers whom the people must not hearken to?
explanation: Hearken not ye to your prophets, nor to your diviners, nor to your dreamers, nor to your enchanters, nor to your sorcerers.

question: In the beginning of whose reign did this word come to Jeremiah?
explanation: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah came this word unto Jeremiah.

question: By whose hand was Jeremiah to send the yokes to the kings?
choices: The messengers who came to Jerusalem
explanation: Send them by the hand of the messengers which come to Jerusalem unto Zedekiah king of Judah.

question: Until what comes shall the nations serve Babylon’s king, his son and his son’s son?
choices: The very time of his land come
explanation: All nations shall serve him, and his son, and his son’s son, until the very time of his land come.

question: Who would perish along with the people if they believed the lie the prophets prophesied in the Lord’s name?
explanation: That ye might perish, ye, and the prophets that prophesy unto you.

question: By whose hand will the Lord consume the nation that will not serve Babylon?
explanation: That nation will I punish, with the sword, and with the famine, and with the pestilence, until I have consumed them by his hand.

question: What did Hananiah say the Lord would bring back to this place within two full years?
choices: The pillars of the temple only
All the vessels of the Lord’s house
explanation: Within two full years will I bring again into this place all the vessels of the LORD’S house, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took away.

question: Whom did Hananiah say the Lord would bring again from Babylon, along with the vessels?
choices: Zedekiah, with the princes of Judah
Jeconiah, with all the captives of Judah
explanation: I will bring again to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, with all the captives of Judah, that went into Babylon.

question: What did Jeremiah first answer to Hananiah’s prophecy?
choices: The Lord has not sent thee
explanation: Jeremiah said, Amen: the LORD do so: the LORD perform thy words which thou hast prophesied.

question: In the beginning of whose reign did Hananiah speak in the house of the Lord?
explanation: In the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, Hananiah spake unto me in the house of the LORD.

question: In whose presence did Hananiah speak to Jeremiah in the house of the Lord?
choices: In a private chamber of the king
At the gate of the city only
In the presence of the priests and all the people
explanation: Hananiah spake unto me in the house of the LORD, in the presence of the priests and of all the people.

question: What did the prophets of old prophesy against many countries and great kingdoms?
explanation: The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.

question: How is a prophet who prophesies peace known to be truly sent by the Lord?
choices: When his word comes to pass
explanation: When the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known, that the LORD hath truly sent him.

question: After Hananiah broke the yoke and spoke again, what did Jeremiah do?
explanation: Hananiah spake in the presence of all the people. And the prophet Jeremiah went his way.

question: Besides the nations, what does the Lord say he has given Nebuchadnezzar?
explanation: I have put a yoke of iron upon the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar; and I have given him the beasts of the field also.

question: Jeremiah said the Lord had not sent Hananiah; what had he made this people do?
explanation: The LORD hath not sent thee; but thou makest this people to trust in a lie.

question: Hananiah said Nebuchadnezzar’s yoke would be broken from whom within two full years?
choices: From the neck of Judah only
From the neck of all nations
explanation: Even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all nations within the space of two full years.

question: What did the Lord say he would do to Hananiah?
choices: Cast him from off the face of the earth
explanation: Behold, I will cast thee from off the face of the earth: this year thou shalt die.

question: What did Jeremiah hope the Lord would perform when he said, The Lord perform thy words?
choices: Bring back the vessels and all the captives from Babylon
explanation: The LORD perform thy words, to bring again the vessels of the LORD’S house, and all that is carried away captive, from Babylon into this place.

question: Hananiah the prophet was the son of whom?
explanation: Hananiah the son of Azur the prophet.

question: Hananiah was from which town?
explanation: Hananiah the son of Azur the prophet, which was of Gibeon.

question: What had Hananiah broken, according to the word the Lord gave Jeremiah?
explanation: Thou hast broken the yokes of wood; but thou shalt make for them yokes of iron.

question: Against whom did the prophets before Jeremiah and Hananiah prophesy?
choices: Against the king of Egypt only
Against many countries and great kingdoms
explanation: The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms.

question: Jeconiah, whom Hananiah promised to bring back, was the son of which king?
explanation: Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah.

question: What happened after Hananiah had broken the yoke from Jeremiah’s neck?
choices: The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah
The princes asked Jeremiah to answer
explanation: Then the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah the prophet, after that Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke from off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah.

question: Why does the Lord say he has put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations?
choices: That they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
That they may be humbled before Egypt
That they may fear the prophets
That they may build the temple
explanation: I have put a yoke of iron upon the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and they shall serve him.

question: What did Jeremiah say to Hananiah about whether the Lord had sent him?
choices: The Lord had sent him to Egypt
The Lord had sent him in a dream
The Lord had sent him with a yoke
The Lord had not sent him
explanation: Hear now, Hananiah; The LORD hath not sent thee.

question: Why did the Lord say Hananiah should die that year?
choices: He taught rebellion against the Lord
He served the king of Babylon
explanation: This year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the LORD.

question: Who carried Jeremiah’s letter to the exiles in Babylon?
explanation: By the hand of Elasah the son of Shaphan, and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent unto Babylon.

question: Why were the exiles told to take wives and have sons and daughters?
choices: That they may be forgotten in Babylon
That they may serve the king
That they may be increased and not diminished
explanation: Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters; that ye may be increased there, and not diminished.

question: What reason does the Lord give for seeking the peace of the city and praying for it?
choices: The king of Babylon will honour them
The city will give them gold
In its peace they shall have peace
The Lord will end the exile sooner
explanation: Seek the peace of the city, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.

question: Whom does the Lord warn the exiles not to let deceive them?
explanation: Let not your prophets and your diviners, that be in the midst of you, deceive you.

question: How does the Lord say the exiles will find him when they seek him?
explanation: Ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.

question: When the exiles call and pray to the Lord, what does he promise?
choices: He will send them a king
He will send a prophet to them
He will turn his face away
explanation: Then shall ye call upon me, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you.

question: To what does the Lord say he will make the king and the people left in Jerusalem like?
choices: Vile figs that cannot be eaten
explanation: I will make them like vile figs, that cannot be eaten, they are so evil.

question: What did the king of Babylon do to Zedekiah and Ahab?
choices: They were drowned in the sea
They were roasted in the fire
explanation: The LORD make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire.

question: Who read Shemaiah’s letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet?
explanation: Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet.

question: Where will the Lord bring the exiles again when he turns away their captivity?
choices: Into the place whence he caused them to be carried away
explanation: I will bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive.

question: Who left Jerusalem with Jeconiah the king?
choices: The priests, the scribes and the singers
The elders, the shepherds and the watchmen
The queen, eunuchs, princes, carpenters and smiths
The judges, the soldiers and the porters
explanation: Jeconiah the king, and the queen, and the eunuchs, the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, and the carpenters, and the smiths, were departed from Jerusalem.

question: Who sent Elasah and Gemariah to Babylon to Nebuchadnezzar?
explanation: Elasah and Gemariah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent unto Babylon to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.

question: What does the Lord say about the prophets and diviners among the exiles?
choices: They prophesy falsely in his name, and he has not sent them
They are sent by the king of Babylon
They prophesy in the name of Baal
explanation: They prophesy falsely unto you in my name: I have not sent them, saith the LORD.

question: What does the Lord say he will do after seventy years are accomplished at Babylon?
choices: Send them a new king from Babylon
Give them the land of Babylon
Raise up Nebuchadrezzar to help them
Visit them and perform his good word, causing them to return
explanation: After seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.

question: From where will the Lord gather the exiles when he turns away their captivity?
choices: From all the nations and all the places where he drove them
explanation: I will gather you from all the nations, and from all the places whither I have driven you, saith the LORD.

question: Besides the king on David’s throne and the people in this city, of whom does the Lord speak with judgment?
choices: Their brethren not gone forth into captivity
explanation: Of the king that sitteth upon the throne of David, and of all the people that dwelleth in this city, and of your brethren that are not gone forth with you into captivity.

question: Why will the Lord send the sword, famine and pestilence and scatter those left in Jerusalem?
choices: They have not hearkened to the words he sent by the prophets
They have not paid tribute to Babylon
They have not kept the sabbath
They have not built the temple
explanation: Because they have not hearkened to my words, which I sent unto them by my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them.

question: What will the Lord do to Ahab and Zedekiah, who prophesy a lie in his name?
choices: He will send them to Egypt
He will make them kings in Babylon
He will bring them home at once
He will deliver them to Nebuchadrezzar, who will slay them
explanation: I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; and he shall slay them before your eyes.

question: What curse shall all the captivity of Judah take up in Babylon?
choices: The Lord make thee like David
The Lord bless thee as Abraham
The Lord make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab
The Lord forget thee as Shiloh
explanation: Of them shall be taken up a curse by all the captivity of Judah which are in Babylon, saying, The LORD make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab.

question: Of what did the Lord say he was a witness against Ahab and Zedekiah?
choices: Villany, adultery and lying words in his name
explanation: They have committed villany in Israel, and have committed adultery with their neighbours’ wives, and have spoken lying words in my name.

question: Besides Zephaniah and all the priests, to whom did Shemaiah send letters in his own name?
explanation: Thou hast sent letters in thy name unto all the people that are at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest.

question: What did Shemaiah say Zephaniah should do to every man who was mad and made himself a prophet?
choices: Put him to death at once
Put him in prison and in the stocks
explanation: That thou shouldest put him in prison, and in the stocks.

question: Whom did Shemaiah say Zephaniah had not reproved for making himself a prophet?
explanation: Why hast thou not reproved Jeremiah of Anathoth, which maketh himself a prophet to you?

question: What did Shemaiah say Jeremiah had sent word to the exiles in Babylon?
choices: That the captivity will end next year
That the captivity is long, so build houses
That the exiles must flee to Egypt
explanation: He sent unto us in Babylon, saying, This captivity is long: build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens.

question: What will the Lord do to Shemaiah the Nehelamite?
choices: He will punish him and his seed
He will make him priest in the temple
He will send him to Egypt
He will give him the land of Babylon
explanation: Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite, and his seed.

question: Elasah, who carried the letter to Babylon, was the son of whom?
explanation: Elasah the son of Shaphan.

question: Gemariah, who carried the letter to Babylon, was the son of whom?
explanation: Gemariah the son of Hilkiah.

question: Ahab, who prophesied a lie in the Lord’s name, was the son of whom?
explanation: Ahab the son of Kolaiah, which prophesy a lie unto you in my name.

question: The false prophet Zedekiah was the son of whom?
explanation: Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, which prophesy a lie unto you in my name.

question: Shemaiah wrote that the Lord had made Zephaniah priest in the stead of whom?
explanation: The LORD hath made thee priest in the stead of Jehoiada the priest.

question: Besides prophets and diviners, what does the Lord tell the exiles not to hearken to?
choices: The words of the temple singers
Their dreams which they cause to be dreamed
explanation: Neither hearken to your dreams which ye cause to be dreamed.

question: To whom was Jeremiah’s letter first addressed among the exiles?
choices: The princes of Judah in Jerusalem
The residue of the elders who were carried away
explanation: The letter that Jeremiah sent unto the residue of the elders which were carried away captives, and to the priests, and to the prophets.

question: The exiles said the Lord had raised up what for them in Babylon?
explanation: Because ye have said, The LORD hath raised us up prophets in Babylon.

question: Among all the nations, what will the Lord make those who remain in Jerusalem?
choices: A blessing, a wonder and a praise
A refuge, a fortress and a tower
A shepherd, a king and a priest
A curse, an astonishment, a hissing and a reproach
explanation: To be a curse, and an astonishment, and an hissing, and a reproach, among all the nations whither I have driven them.

question: To whom was Jeremiah to send word about Shemaiah the Nehelamite?
explanation: Send to all them of the captivity, saying, Thus saith the LORD concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite.

question: What shall Shemaiah not behold?
choices: The good that the Lord will do for his people
explanation: Neither shall he behold the good that I will do for my people, saith the LORD.

question: Who does the Lord say caused the exiles to be carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon?
explanation: Unto all that are carried away captives, whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem unto Babylon.

question: Before whose eyes shall Nebuchadrezzar slay Ahab and Zedekiah?
choices: Before the temple of the Lord
Before the eyes of the exiles
explanation: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; and he shall slay them before your eyes.

question: In whose name did Shemaiah send letters to the people at Jerusalem?
choices: In the name of the Lord
In the name of the king
explanation: Because thou hast sent letters in thy name unto all the people that are at Jerusalem.

question: What does the Lord say about whether he sent Shemaiah, who caused the exiles to trust in a lie?
choices: The Lord had sent him in a dream
The Lord had not sent him
The Lord had sent him to Babylon
The Lord had sent him to the priests
explanation: Shemaiah hath prophesied unto you, and I sent him not, and he caused you to trust in a lie.

question: Where will the Lord cause his people to return when he brings back their captivity?
choices: The land he gave to their fathers
explanation: I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.

question: Whom shall the people serve when their yoke is broken?
choices: The Lord their God and David their king
explanation: They shall serve the LORD their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.

question: The Lord says he will save Jacob and his seed from where?
explanation: Fear thou not, O my servant Jacob: for, lo, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity.

question: What will happen to all that devour Zion?
explanation: All they that devour thee shall be devoured.

question: What will the Lord restore to Zion?
choices: Health, and healing of his wounds
explanation: I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the LORD.

question: What did the enemies call Zion, saying no man seeketh after her?
explanation: They called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after.

question: On whom shall the whirlwind of the Lord fall with pain?
explanation: The whirlwind of the LORD goeth forth with fury, a continuing whirlwind: it shall fall with pain upon the head of the wicked.

question: What kind of voice does the Lord say they have heard?
choices: A voice of rejoicing and singing
A voice of war and triumph
A voice of trembling and fear, and not of peace
A voice of weeping and mourning
explanation: We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.

question: Besides breaking the yoke from Jacob’s neck, what will the Lord do to his bonds?
explanation: I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds.

question: Though it is the time of Jacob’s trouble, what does the Lord say of Jacob?
choices: He shall be saved out of it
He shall be taken to Babylon
explanation: It is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.

question: Though he makes a full end of the nations, how will the Lord deal with Jacob?
choices: He will make a full end of them
He will correct them in measure
explanation: I will not make a full end of thee: but I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished.

question: Zion’s bruise is incurable; what does the Lord say there is none to do?
explanation: There is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines.

question: What have all of Zion’s lovers done?
choices: Her lovers have returned to her
Her lovers have gone to war
Her lovers have given her gold
explanation: All thy lovers have forgotten thee; they seek thee not.

question: Why does the Lord say he has wounded Zion with the wound of an enemy?
choices: The sins of her kings only
explanation: I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, for the multitude of thine iniquity; because thy sins were increased.

question: What will happen to all of Zion’s adversaries?
explanation: All thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity.

question: Upon what shall the city be builded when the Lord brings back the captivity of Jacob’s tents?
explanation: The city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.

question: What shall proceed out of the people when the Lord restores them?
choices: Thanksgiving and the voice of them that make merry
explanation: Out of them shall proceed thanksgiving and the voice of them that make merry.

question: What will the Lord do with the people, so that they are not few and not small?
choices: They shall not be few or small
They shall be hidden from their enemies
They shall be kings of Babylon
explanation: I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also glorify them, and they shall not be small.

question: From where will the governor of the restored people proceed?
explanation: Their nobles shall be of themselves, and their governor shall proceed from the midst of them.

question: What will the Lord bring again, having mercy on Jacob’s dwellingplaces?
explanation: I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces.

question: What shall remain after the manner thereof when the city is builded?
explanation: The city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.

question: What does the Lord say about the children and the congregation of the restored people?
choices: Their congregation shall be established before him
Their congregation shall go to Egypt
explanation: Their children also shall be as aforetime, and their congregation shall be established before me.

question: When Jacob returns and is in rest and quiet, what does the Lord say?
explanation: Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid.

question: What does the Lord say he will cause the governor to do?
choices: He will send him to Babylon
He will make him king over the nations
He will cause him to draw near and approach unto him
He will hide him in the wilderness
explanation: I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me.

question: Who shall no more serve themselves of Jacob when his yoke is broken?
explanation: Strangers shall no more serve themselves of him.

question: How long shall the fierce anger of the Lord not return?
choices: Until he has performed the intents of his heart
Until the king of Babylon falls
explanation: The fierce anger of the LORD shall not return, until he have done it, and until he have performed the intents of his heart.

question: The Lord will not make a full end of Jacob, but of whom will he make a full end?
choices: The nations of the north only
All the nations where he scattered Jacob
explanation: Though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee.

question: What will happen to those who spoil Zion?
explanation: They that spoil thee shall be a spoil, and all that prey upon thee will I give for a prey.

question: What does the Lord say of the day of Jacob’s trouble?
explanation: Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it.

question: Whose captivity will the Lord bring again when he causes them to return to the land?
explanation: I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah.

question: What question does the Lord ask Jeremiah to ask, since every man holds his hands on his loins?
choices: Whether a king doth reign without a throne
Whether a shepherd doth leave his flock
Whether a prophet doth dream by night
Whether a man doth travail with child
explanation: Ask ye now, and see whether a man doth travail with child? wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins, as a woman in travail?

question: Where was a voice of lamentation and bitter weeping heard?
explanation: A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping; Rahel weeping for her children.

question: Where did the people left of the sword find grace?
explanation: The people which were left of the sword found grace in the wilderness; even Israel, when I went to cause him to rest.

question: Whom does the Lord call his firstborn?
explanation: I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.

question: He that scattered Israel will gather and keep him, as what?
explanation: He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.

question: To what shall the soul of the returned people be like?
explanation: Their soul shall be as a watered garden; and they shall not sorrow any more at all.

question: Into what will the Lord turn their mourning?
explanation: I will turn their mourning into joy, and will comfort them, and make them rejoice from their sorrow.

question: How did Ephraim describe himself when the Lord chastised him?
choices: A bullock unaccustomed to the yoke
A lamb led to the slaughter
explanation: Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised, as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke.

question: Who will return with the great company, together with the woman with child?
explanation: I will gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together.

question: What saying shall they use no more in those days?
choices: The shepherd is smitten and the sheep are scattered
The sun shall be darkened and the moon turned to blood
The fathers have eaten a sour grape
The wise man is gone and the fool remains
explanation: In those days they shall say no more, The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children’s teeth are set on edge.

question: What does the Lord say about every one who eats the sour grape?
choices: Every man shall die for the sins of the king
Every man shall die for his own iniquity
Every man shall live for his father’s sake
Every man shall be saved by sacrifice
explanation: Every one shall die for his own iniquity: every man that eateth the sour grape, his teeth shall be set on edge.

question: What will the Lord be to the families of Israel at the same time?
choices: The God of all the families of Israel
The King of all the nations
The Shepherd of the north only
explanation: At the same time, saith the LORD, will I be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.

question: What shall the planters plant, eating of it as a common thing?
choices: Wheat in the valley of Hinnom
Vines upon the mountains of Samaria
explanation: Thou shalt yet plant vines upon the mountains of Samaria: the planters shall plant, and shall eat them as common things.

question: What shall the watchmen upon Mount Ephraim cry?
choices: Arise, and let us go down to Egypt
Arise, and let us go up to Zion
Arise, and let us build the wall
explanation: The watchmen upon the mount Ephraim shall cry, Arise ye, and let us go up to Zion unto the LORD our God.

question: From where will the Lord bring his people and gather them?
choices: From the north country and the coasts of the earth
From the wilderness and the sea
explanation: I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth.

question: Where will the Lord cause them to walk so that they do not stumble?
choices: By the rivers of waters, in a straight way
Through the sea on dry land
explanation: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble.

question: The Lord redeemed and ransomed Jacob from what?
choices: From the mouth of the lion
From the pit of the grave
From the hand of him that was stronger than he
explanation: The LORD hath redeemed Jacob, and ransomed him from the hand of him that was stronger than he.

question: What goods will they flow together to the goodness of the Lord for?
choices: Wheat, wine, oil, and the young of the flock and herd
explanation: They shall flow together to the goodness of the LORD, for wheat, and for wine, and for oil, and for the young of the flock and of the herd.

question: Whose soul will the Lord satiate with fatness?
explanation: I will satiate the soul of the priests with fatness, and my people shall be satisfied with my goodness.

question: Why is Rachel told to refrain her voice from weeping?
choices: Her king shall be raised up
explanation: Refrain thy voice from weeping: for thy work shall be rewarded, saith the LORD; and they shall come again from the land of the enemy.

question: After he was turned and instructed, why was Ephraim ashamed and confounded?
choices: He bore the reproach of his youth
explanation: I was ashamed, yea, even confounded, because I did bear the reproach of my youth.

question: What does the Lord say he will do for Ephraim, whom he still earnestly remembers?
choices: He will leave him in Babylon
He will surely have mercy upon him
He will make him a servant
explanation: My bowels are troubled for him; I will surely have mercy upon him, saith the LORD.

question: What is the virgin of Israel told to set up for her return?
explanation: Set thee up waymarks, make thee high heaps: set thine heart toward the highway.

question: Who shall dwell in Judah and all the cities thereof together?
choices: Husbandmen and they that go forth with flocks
explanation: There shall dwell in Judah itself, and in all the cities thereof together, husbandmen, and they that go forth with flocks.

question: With what will the Lord sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah?
choices: With the seed of man and the seed of beast
explanation: I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man, and with the seed of beast.

question: As the Lord watched over them to pluck up and break down, how will he now watch over them?
choices: To pluck up and break down
explanation: So will I watch over them, to build, and to plant, saith the LORD.

question: The new covenant will not be like the one made when?
choices: The day he gave the law on Sinai
The day he took them by the hand out of the land of Egypt
The day he brought them over Jordan
The day David was anointed king
explanation: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt.

question: Although they broke the covenant, what does the Lord say he was unto them?
explanation: Which my covenant they brake, although I was an husband unto them, saith the LORD.

question: Why will no one need to teach his neighbour, saying, Know the LORD?
choices: They shall all read the law
They shall all know the Lord, from the least to the greatest
explanation: They shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the LORD.

question: What does the Lord promise about their sin in the new covenant?
choices: He will forgive only the priests
He will punish their sin in measure
He will forgive iniquity and remember sin no more
He will hide their sin for seventy years
explanation: I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.

question: What is the name of the Lord who divides the sea when the waves roar?
explanation: Which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The LORD of hosts is his name.

question: If the ordinances of the sun, moon and stars depart, what will happen?
choices: The seed of Israel would cease from being a nation
The land would be given to strangers
explanation: If those ordinances depart from before me, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.

question: When will the Lord cast off all the seed of Israel for what they have done?
choices: If the sun stands still at noon
If the sea rises above the mountains
If the king of Babylon is slain
If heaven above can be measured
explanation: If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, I will also cast off all the seed of Israel.

question: From which tower shall the city be built to the Lord to the gate of the corner?
explanation: The city shall be built to the LORD from the tower of Hananeel unto the gate of the corner.

question: Over which hill shall the measuring line go forth?
explanation: The measuring line shall yet go forth over against it upon the hill Gareb, and shall compass about to Goath.

question: What shall the whole valley of the dead bodies and of the ashes be?
explanation: The whole valley of the dead bodies, and of the ashes, shall be holy unto the LORD; it shall not be plucked up, nor thrown down any more for ever.

question: The fields of the holy valley reach to which brook?
explanation: All the fields unto the brook of Kidron, unto the corner of the horse gate toward the east.

question: Where is Israel told to shout, singing with gladness for Jacob?
choices: Among the chief of the nations
explanation: Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations.

question: Where are the nations told to declare that he who scattered Israel will gather him?
explanation: Hear the word of the LORD, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off.

question: What did Ephraim pray, saying the Lord is his God?
choices: Turn thou me, and I shall be turned
Heal thou me, and I shall be healed
Save thou me, and I shall live
Teach thou me, and I shall learn
explanation: Turn thou me, and I shall be turned; for thou art the LORD my God.

question: How does the Lord say his people will come back, and how will he lead them?
choices: They shall come with songs and harps
They shall come with weeping and supplications
explanation: They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them.

question: Who had shut Jeremiah up in the court of the prison?
explanation: Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, Wherefore dost thou prophesy?

question: Who came to Jeremiah in the court of the prison and asked him to buy a field?
explanation: Hanameel mine uncle’s son came to me in the court of the prison, and said unto me, Buy my field, I pray thee.

question: How much money did Jeremiah weigh out for the field?
explanation: I bought the field of Hanameel my uncle’s son, and weighed him the money, even seventeen shekels of silver.

question: To whom did Jeremiah give the evidence of the purchase?
explanation: I gave the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah.

question: Why had Zedekiah shut Jeremiah up?
choices: He had spoken against the priests
He had refused to pay tribute
That the city would be given to Babylon
explanation: Wherefore dost thou prophesy, and say, Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it?

question: What would Zedekiah do when delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon?
choices: He shall make a covenant with Egypt
He shall speak with him mouth to mouth
explanation: Zedekiah shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him mouth to mouth, and his eyes shall behold his eyes.

question: By what did Jeremiah say the Lord made the heaven and the earth?
choices: By the counsel of the prophets
By his great power and stretched out arm
By the hand of the king
By the sword of the Chaldeans
explanation: Thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm.

question: To whom did they offer incense upon the roofs of their houses?
explanation: The houses upon whose roofs they have offered incense unto Baal, and poured out drink offerings unto other gods.

question: To whom did they cause their sons and daughters to pass through the fire?
explanation: They built the high places of Baal, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech.

question: What will the Lord make with them so that he will not turn away from doing them good?
explanation: I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from them, to do them good.

question: Where was the court of the prison in which Jeremiah was shut up?
choices: In the temple of the Lord
In the king of Judah’s house
explanation: Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the king of Judah’s house.

question: What right made Jeremiah the one to buy his cousin’s field?
choices: The right of the firstborn only
explanation: The right of inheritance is thine, and the redemption is thine; buy it for thyself.

question: Where was the field at Anathoth that Hanameel offered?
choices: In the hill country of Ephraim
explanation: Buy my field that is in Anathoth, which is in the country of Benjamin.

question: When Hanameel came to the court of the prison, what did Jeremiah then know?
choices: That the king had sent him
That the city would soon fall
That it was the word of the Lord
explanation: Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.

question: What two copies of the evidence of the purchase did Jeremiah take?
choices: One for the king and one for the priests
One of gold and one of silver
explanation: I took the evidence of the purchase, both that which was sealed according to the law and custom, and that which was open.

question: Why were the evidences to be put in an earthen vessel?
choices: That they may continue many days
That they may be sold to Babylon
That they may be read in the temple
That they may be buried with the king
explanation: Put them in an earthen vessel, that they may continue many days.

question: In Jeremiah’s prayer, to whom does the Lord show lovingkindness?
choices: Unto the kings of the earth
Unto the nations of the north
explanation: Thou shewest lovingkindness unto thousands.

question: From where did the Lord bring Israel with signs, wonders, a strong hand and great terror?
choices: Out of the land of Babylon
Out of the wilderness of Sinai
Out of the land of Egypt
Out of the cities of Edom
explanation: Thou hast brought forth thy people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs, and with wonders, and with a strong hand.

question: What kind of land did the Lord swear to their fathers to give them?
choices: A land of wheat and barley
A land flowing with milk and honey
A land of rivers and lakes
explanation: Thou hast given them this land, which thou didst swear to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.

question: Why did the Lord cause all this evil to come upon the people who possessed the land?
choices: They obeyed not his voice and walked not in his law
explanation: They obeyed not thy voice, neither walked in thy law; therefore thou hast caused all this evil to come upon them.

question: Because of what is the city given into the hand of the Chaldeans?
choices: The flood, the fire and the hail
The drought, the locust and the storm
The exile, the silence and the fear
The sword, the famine and the pestilence
explanation: The city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans, because of the sword, and of the famine, and of the pestilence.

question: Though the city was given to the Chaldeans, what had the Lord told Jeremiah to do?
choices: Go down to Egypt and wait
Buy the field for money and take witnesses
Write the evidence in a book
explanation: Thou hast said unto me, O Lord GOD, Buy thee the field for money, and take witnesses; for the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.

question: What does the Lord call himself when he asks, Is there any thing too hard for me?
choices: The God of the heavens only
explanation: Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?

question: What will the Chaldeans do to Jerusalem and its houses?
choices: They shall set fire on the city and burn it
They shall carry it to Babylon
They shall plow it like a field
explanation: The Chaldeans shall come and set fire on this city, and burn it with the houses.

question: What will the Lord do with those he drove out of all countries in his anger?
choices: He will leave them in the nations
He will send them to Egypt
He will make them servants of Babylon
He will gather them and bring them again to dwell safely
explanation: I will gather them out of all countries, and I will bring them again unto this place, and I will cause them to dwell safely.

question: Hanameel was the son of which man, Jeremiah’s uncle?
explanation: Hanameel the son of Shallum thine uncle shall come unto thee.

question: Baruch, who received the evidence, was the son of whom?
explanation: Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah.

question: Before whom did Jeremiah give the evidence to Baruch, besides the witnesses?
choices: All the Jews that sat in the court of the prison
explanation: In the presence of the witnesses that subscribed the book of the purchase, before all the Jews that sat in the court of the prison.

question: Where would the king of Babylon lead Zedekiah, to stay until the Lord visited him?
explanation: He shall lead Zedekiah to Babylon, and there shall he be until I visit him, saith the LORD.

question: In which land, besides places around Jerusalem, shall men buy fields and seal evidences?
explanation: Men shall buy fields for money, and subscribe evidences, and seal them, and take witnesses in the land of Benjamin.

question: Jeremiah calls the Lord the Great, the Mighty God; what is his name?
explanation: The Great, the Mighty God, the LORD of hosts, is his name.

question: Where does the Lord recompense the iniquity of the fathers?
choices: Into the bosom of their children after them
Into the hand of the king
Into the house of the priests
explanation: Thou recompensest the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them.

question: Where did they build the high places of Baal?
choices: In the valley of the son of Hinnom
explanation: They built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom.

question: Where did they set their abominations, to defile it?
choices: In the court of the prison
In the house which is called by his name
explanation: They set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to defile it.

question: They have turned what unto the Lord, and not the face?
explanation: They have turned unto me the back, and not the face.

question: What has this city been to the Lord from the day they built it?
choices: A provocation of his anger and fury
explanation: This city hath been to me as a provocation of mine anger and of my fury from the day that they built it.

question: What will the Lord put in their hearts so that they shall not depart from him?
explanation: I will put my fear in their hearts, that they shall not depart from me.

question: Like as the Lord brought all this great evil upon the people, what will he do?
choices: So will he bring them peace in a year
So will he bring Babylon down at once
So will he bring all the good he has promised
So will he bring a famine
explanation: Like as I have brought all this great evil upon this people, so will I bring upon them all the good that I have promised them.

question: How will the Lord plant them in this land assuredly?
choices: With his whole heart and whole soul
With the help of the nations
explanation: I will plant them in this land assuredly with my whole heart and with my whole soul.

question: Besides their kings, princes, priests and prophets, who else provoked the Lord?
choices: The men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem
explanation: Their kings, their princes, their priests, and their prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

question: Where was Jeremiah when the word of the Lord came to him the second time?
choices: In the court of the prison
In the temple of the Lord
explanation: The word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah the second time, while he was yet shut up in the court of the prison.

question: What does the Lord say he will bring to the city?
explanation: Behold, I will bring it health and cure, and I will cure them.

question: What will the Lord do with the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel?
choices: He will send them to Egypt
He will cause them to return
He will leave them in Babylon
explanation: I will cause the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel to return, and will build them, as at the first.

question: What will the Lord do about the sins by which the people have sinned against him?
choices: He will send them more prophets
He will cleanse them from all their iniquity
explanation: I will cleanse them from all their iniquity, whereby they have sinned against me.

question: What shall David never want?
choices: A man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel
explanation: David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel.

question: What are the priests the Levites to offer before the Lord?
choices: Burnt offerings, meat offerings and sacrifice continually
explanation: Neither shall the priests the Levites want a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to kindle meat offerings, and to do sacrifice continually.

question: To what does the Lord liken the seed of David and the Levites he will multiply?
choices: The stars and the dust of the earth
The waves of the sea and the leaves of trees
The host of heaven and the sand of the sea
The birds of the air and the fish of the sea
explanation: As the host of heaven cannot be numbered, neither the sand of the sea measured: so will I multiply the seed of David my servant.

question: By what name shall Jerusalem be called?
explanation: This is the name wherewith she shall be called, The LORD our righteousness.

question: Besides the houses of this city, whose houses are thrown down by the mounts and by the sword?
choices: The houses of the kings of Judah
explanation: Concerning the houses of this city, and concerning the houses of the kings of Judah, which are thrown down by the mounts, and by the sword.

question: Why has the Lord hid his face from this city?
choices: For the sins of the king alone
explanation: For all whose wickedness I have hid my face from this city.

question: How will the Lord build Judah and Israel when their captivity returns?
choices: As in the days of Solomon
As in the days of Moses
As in the days of the judges
explanation: I will cause the captivity to return, and will build them, as at the first.

question: What shall the restored city be to the Lord before all the nations of the earth?
choices: A name of terror and a curse
A name of joy, a praise and an honour
A name of silence and shame
A name of war and strength
explanation: It shall be to me a name of joy, a praise and an honour before all the nations of the earth.

question: What shall the nations do when they hear all the good the Lord does for his people?
choices: They shall fear and tremble at the goodness
They shall rage against the Lord
They shall make war against the city
explanation: They shall fear and tremble for all the goodness and for all the prosperity that I procure unto it.

question: Where shall the voice of joy and gladness again be heard, where it was desolate without man and beast?
choices: In the desolate cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem
explanation: There shall be heard in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, that are desolate.

question: What shall the people say as they praise the Lord of hosts?
choices: The LORD is a rock; his strength is sure
The LORD is King; his kingdom is for ever
The LORD is good; his mercy endureth for ever
The LORD is holy; his name is great
explanation: Praise the LORD of hosts: for the LORD is good; for his mercy endureth for ever.

question: What shall they bring into the house of the Lord?
explanation: They shall bring the sacrifice of praise into the house of the LORD.

question: Under whose hands shall the flocks pass again in the cities of Judah?
explanation: Shall the flocks pass again under the hands of him that telleth them, saith the LORD.

question: What shall happen to Judah and Jerusalem in those days?
choices: Israel shall be saved and Jerusalem shall be destroyed
Judah shall be carried away and Jerusalem shall be silent
Judah shall rule the nations and Jerusalem shall pay tribute
Judah shall be saved and Jerusalem shall dwell safely
explanation: In those days shall Judah be saved, and Jerusalem shall dwell safely.

question: What had this people spoken about the two families which the Lord had chosen?
choices: He hath sent them to Babylon
explanation: The two families which the LORD hath chosen, he hath even cast them off.

question: Over whom would David’s seed be rulers, if the Lord cast away the seed of Jacob?
choices: The seed of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
explanation: I will not take any of his seed to be rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

question: Instead of casting away the seed of Jacob, what will the Lord do?
choices: Cause their captivity to return and have mercy on them
explanation: I will cause their captivity to return, and have mercy on them.

question: How does the Lord describe himself as the maker of the city?
choices: The Lord that sent the prophets
The Lord that led them out of Egypt
The Lord that sits on the cherubim
The Lord that formed it, to establish it
explanation: Thus saith the LORD the maker thereof, the LORD that formed it, to establish it; the LORD is his name.

question: With what will the Lord fill the houses when they come to fight with the Chaldeans?
choices: The dead bodies of men whom he has slain
explanation: They come to fight with the Chaldeans, but it is to fill them with the dead bodies of men, whom I have slain in mine anger and in my fury.

question: Besides joy and gladness, whose voices shall again be heard in the desolate places?
choices: The voice of the shepherd and the voice of the flock
The voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride
The voice of the king and the voice of the priest
The voice of the watchman and the voice of the trumpet
explanation: The voice of joy, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride.

question: In which land, among the places about Jerusalem, shall the flocks pass again?
explanation: In the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, shall the flocks pass again.

question: Whom does the Lord call his servant, with whom the covenant cannot be broken?
explanation: Then may also my covenant be broken with David my servant.

question: With whom, besides David, would the Lord’s covenant be broken if day and night could cease?
choices: The Levites the priests, his ministers
explanation: My covenant be broken with David my servant, and with the Levites the priests, my ministers.

question: What shall again be in the place that is desolate without man and beast?
explanation: Again in this place, which is desolate without man and without beast, shall be an habitation of shepherds causing their flocks to lie down.

question: What does the Lord say he has appointed, along with the covenant of day and night?
choices: The ordinances of heaven and earth
explanation: If my covenant be not with day and night, and if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth.

question: If the covenant of day and night could be broken, what would be broken with David?
choices: That he should not rule over Babylon
That he should not build the temple
That he should not be remembered
That he should not have a son to reign upon his throne
explanation: Then may also my covenant be broken with David my servant, that he should not have a son to reign upon his throne.

question: To whom has the Lord promised the good thing he will perform?
choices: The kings of Egypt and Babylon
The house of Israel and the house of Judah
explanation: I will perform that good thing which I have promised unto the house of Israel and to the house of Judah.

question: What shall the Branch of righteousness execute in the land?
choices: Peace and plenty in the temple
Judgment and righteousness in the land
explanation: The Branch of righteousness shall grow up unto David; and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land.

question: Besides answering, what does the Lord promise to show Jeremiah when he calls?
choices: Great and mighty things, which thou knowest not
The names of the kings of Babylon
explanation: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.

question: Unto whom will the Lord cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up?
explanation: In those days, and at that time, will I cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up unto David.

question: Whom does God say have dealt treacherously with Jeremiah?
choices: His brethren and the house of his father
explanation: Even thy brethren, and the house of thy father, even they have dealt treacherously with thee.

question: What will those who sowed wheat reap instead?
explanation: They have sown wheat, but shall reap thorns: they shall be ashamed of their revenues because of the fierce anger of the LORD.

question: What will God do after he has plucked his people out of their land?
choices: Return, have compassion and bring each man to his heritage
explanation: After I have plucked them out I will return, and have compassion on them, and will bring them again, every man to his heritage.

question: What will God do to a nation that will not obey?
choices: Send a prophet to it again
Utterly pluck it up and destroy it
explanation: If they will not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation, saith the LORD.

question: How does Jeremiah ask God to treat the wicked?
choices: Pull them out like sheep for the slaughter
Drive them out like wild asses
explanation: Pull them out like sheep for the slaughter, and prepare them for the day of slaughter.

question: What does God say his heritage has become to him?
choices: A lion in the forest that cries out against him
explanation: Mine heritage is unto me as a lion in the forest; it crieth out against me: therefore have I hated it.

question: Who have destroyed and trodden down the Lord’s vineyard?
explanation: Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have trodden my portion under foot.

question: Why does the land mourn and the herbs of every field wither?
choices: Because of the wickedness of those who live there
Because the rivers have dried up
Because no rain came for years
explanation: How long shall the land mourn, and the herbs of every field wither, for the wickedness of them that dwell therein?

question: By whom had the evil neighbours taught God’s people to swear?
explanation: They taught my people to swear by Baal; they must learn to swear by my name, The LORD liveth.

question: How far will the sword of the LORD devour?
choices: From one end of the land to the other
Only to the gates of Jerusalem
explanation: The sword of the LORD shall devour from the one end of the land even to the other end of the land: no flesh shall have peace.

question: What does God say he will do to the evil neighbours who touch his people’s inheritance?
choices: Pluck them out of their land
explanation: Behold, I will pluck them out of their land, and pluck out the house of Judah from among them.

question: Why shall the people be ashamed of their revenues?
choices: Because of the fierce anger of the LORD
explanation: They shall be ashamed of your revenues because of the fierce anger of the LORD.

question: What does Jeremiah say God has seen and tried?
explanation: But thou, O LORD, knowest me: thou hast seen me, and tried mine heart toward thee.

question: What does God compare his heritage to when the birds round about are against her?
explanation: Mine heritage is unto me as a speckled bird, the birds round about are against her.

question: What did the wicked say, according to Jeremiah, about their end?
choices: He shall not see our last end
explanation: The beasts are consumed, and the birds; because they said, He shall not see our last end.

question: Where have the spoilers come?
choices: Upon all high places through the wilderness
explanation: The spoilers are come upon all high places through the wilderness.

question: Into whose hand has God given “the dearly beloved of my soul”?
explanation: I have given the dearly beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies.

question: What must the neighbour nations do to be built in the midst of God’s people?
choices: Learn his people’s ways, swear by his name
explanation: If they will diligently learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, then shall they be built in the midst of my people.

question: What kind of words are Jeremiah’s brethren said to speak, which he must not believe?
explanation: Believe them not, though they speak fair words unto thee.

question: What have many pastors made of God’s pleasant portion?
explanation: They have made my pleasant portion a desolate wilderness.

question: Why is the whole land made desolate?
choices: Because no man lays it to heart
explanation: The whole land is made desolate, because no man layeth it to heart.

question: What do the wicked do after God has planted them?
choices: Take root, grow and bring forth fruit
explanation: Thou hast planted them, yea, they have taken root: they grow, yea, they bring forth fruit.

question: What did Jeremiah do when the Lord told him to get a linen girdle?
choices: He sold it in the market
He got it and put it on his loins
He gave it to the king
explanation: So I got a girdle according to the word of the LORD, and put it on my loins.

question: What was Jeremiah told not to do with the linen girdle?
explanation: Go and get thee a linen girdle, and put it upon thy loins, and put it not in water.

question: Where did Jeremiah go to hide the girdle?
explanation: I went, and hid it by Euphrates, as the LORD commanded me.

question: What did the Lord say he would mar, as the girdle was marred?
choices: The pride of Judah and Jerusalem
explanation: After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.

question: What did the Lord say every bottle would be filled with?
explanation: Every bottle shall be filled with wine: and they shall say, Do we not certainly know that every bottle shall be filled with wine?

question: Whom will the Lord fill with drunkenness?
choices: Everyone in the land, kings, priests and prophets
explanation: I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, even the kings that sit upon David’s throne, and the priests, and the prophets, with drunkenness.

question: What should the people do before the Lord brings darkness?
choices: Give glory to the LORD their God
explanation: Give glory to the LORD your God, before he cause darkness, and before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains.

question: Why will Jeremiah’s eye weep sore and run down with tears?
choices: Because the LORD’S flock is carried away captive
Because he is in the stocks
explanation: Mine eye shall weep sore, and run down with tears, because the LORD’S flock is carried away captive.

question: What will the Lord scatter the people like?
choices: Stubble blown by the wind of the wilderness
explanation: Therefore will I scatter them as the stubble that passeth away by the wind of the wilderness.

question: Whom does the Lord say will be like the useless girdle?
choices: The evil people who refuse to hear his words
explanation: This evil people, which refuse to hear my words, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.

question: Whom had the Lord caused to cleave to him, as a girdle cleaves to a man?
choices: The whole house of Israel and of Judah
explanation: As the girdle cleaveth to the loins of a man, so have I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah.

question: What will the Lord do to the fathers and the sons?
explanation: I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.

question: Whom does Jeremiah tell to “Humble yourselves, sit down”?
explanation: Say unto the king and to the queen, Humble yourselves, sit down: for your principalities shall come down.

question: What will the Lord turn the light into, while they look for it?
choices: The shadow of death and gross darkness
explanation: While ye look for light, he turn it into the shadow of death, and make it gross darkness.

question: Which cities will be shut up so that none can open them?
explanation: The cities of the south shall be shut up, and none shall open them.

question: What reason does the Lord give for the lot that has come on Jerusalem?
choices: She forgot him and trusted in falsehood
explanation: This is thy lot, from me, saith the LORD; because thou hast forgotten me, and trusted in falsehood.

question: Why are Jerusalem’s skirts discovered and her heels made bare?
choices: For the greatness of her iniquity
explanation: For the greatness of thine iniquity are thy skirts discovered, and thy heels made bare.

question: Where has the Lord seen Jerusalem’s abominations?
choices: On the hills in the fields
In the courts of the temple
explanation: I have seen thine adulteries, and thine abominations on the hills in the fields.

question: From what direction do those come whom Jeremiah tells Judah to look at?
explanation: Lift up your eyes, and behold them that come from the north: where is the flock that was given thee?

question: What question does the Lord end with for Jerusalem?
choices: When shall she be made clean?
What will she say to Babylon?
explanation: Woe unto thee, O Jerusalem! wilt thou not be made clean? when shall it once be?

question: What will the people say when told every bottle shall be filled with wine?
choices: Do we not certainly know it?
explanation: They shall say unto thee, Do we not certainly know that every bottle shall be filled with wine?

question: Though the Lord made them cleave to him, what would the people not do?
explanation: That they might be unto me for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory: but they would not hear.

question: What question may Jerusalem ask in her heart when punished?
choices: Wherefore come these things upon me?
explanation: If thou say in thine heart, Wherefore come these things upon me? For the greatness of thine iniquity are thy skirts discovered.

question: In what was the girdle hidden by Euphrates?
explanation: Arise, go to Euphrates, and hide it there in a hole of the rock.

question: What did Jeremiah do to get the girdle back?
explanation: I went to Euphrates, and digged, and took the girdle from the place where I had hid it.

question: What will come down, even the crown of your glory?
explanation: Humble yourselves, sit down: for your principalities shall come down, even the crown of your glory.

question: Where will the Lord’s soul weep for their pride?
explanation: If ye will not hear it, my soul shall weep in secret places for your pride.

question: What have the people taught others to be over them?
explanation: What wilt thou say when he shall punish thee? for thou hast taught them to be captains, and as chief over thee.

question: Upon what shall their feet stumble if they do not give glory?
explanation: Give glory to the LORD your God, before he cause darkness, and before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains.

question: What reason is given for “be not proud”?
explanation: Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the LORD hath spoken.

question: How does the Lord compare the sorrows that will take Jerusalem?
explanation: Shall not sorrows take thee, as a woman in travail?

question: What does the Lord say the people walk after, which makes them like the girdle?
explanation: Walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.

question: When did the Lord send Jeremiah back to take the girdle?
explanation: And it came to pass after many days, that the LORD said unto me, Arise, go to Euphrates, and take the girdle from thence.

question: Besides abominations, what has the Lord seen in Jerusalem?
explanation: I have seen thine adulteries, and thy neighings, the lewdness of thy whoredom, and thine abominations on the hills in the fields.

question: What do the people walk in, according to the Lord?
explanation: This evil people walk in the imagination of their heart.

question: What will the Lord do with Jerusalem’s skirts so that her shame appears?
explanation: Therefore will I discover thy skirts upon thy face, that thy shame may appear.

question: What will the Lord not do when he destroys the fathers and sons?
explanation: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.

question: Who covered their heads in shame because the ground was chapt and there was no rain?
explanation: Because the ground is chapt, for there was no rain in the earth, the plowmen were ashamed, they covered their heads.

question: Where did the nobles send their little ones, and what did they find?
choices: To the temple, but it was shut
To Egypt, but there was no bread
To the hills, but found only wolves
To the waters, but they found no water
explanation: Their nobles have sent their little ones to the waters: they came to the pits, and found no water; they returned with their vessels empty.

question: What does the Lord tell Jeremiah not to do?
choices: Pray for this people for their good
explanation: Then said the LORD unto me, Pray not for this people for their good.

question: What will the Lord do when the people fast?
choices: He will heal them at once
He will not hear their cry
explanation: When they fast, I will not hear their cry; and when they offer burnt offering and an oblation, I will not accept them.

question: What will happen to the prophets who say sword and famine shall not come?
choices: They shall be honoured by the king
They shall be consumed by sword and famine
explanation: By sword and famine shall those prophets be consumed.

question: Who alone can give rain, according to the people’s final cry?
explanation: Are there any among the vanities of the Gentiles that can cause rain? art not thou he, O LORD our God? therefore we will wait upon thee.

question: What does the Lord say of the prophets who prophesy in his name?
choices: He did not send them or speak to them
He sent them to the king
He taught them in the temple
explanation: The prophets prophesy lies in my name: I sent them not, neither have I commanded them, neither spake unto them.

question: What will happen to the people who listen to the false prophets?
choices: They will be cast out in the streets with none to bury them
They will be taken to Egypt
explanation: The people to whom they prophesy shall be cast out in the streets of Jerusalem because of the famine and the sword; and they shall have none to bury them.

question: What does Jeremiah fear God has become, like a wayfaring man?
choices: A stranger in the land who tarries for a night
explanation: Why shouldest thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man that turneth aside to tarry for a night?

question: What did the hind do in the field because there was no grass?
explanation: The hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass.

question: Why does the Lord not accept the people?
choices: They have loved to wander and not refrained their feet
explanation: Thus have they loved to wander, they have not refrained their feet, therefore the LORD doth not accept them.

question: What does Jeremiah ask the Lord not to do to his covenant?
explanation: Do not abhor us, for thy name’s sake: remember, break not thy covenant with us.

question: What does Jeremiah see when he goes out into the field and into the city?
choices: The slain with the sword and the sick with famine
explanation: If I go forth into the field, then behold the slain with the sword! and if I enter into the city, then behold them that are sick with famine!

question: For whose sake do the people ask the Lord to act, though their iniquities testify against them?
explanation: O LORD, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name’s sake.

question: What does Jeremiah say is broken with a great breach?
choices: The virgin daughter of his people
explanation: The virgin daughter of my people is broken with a great breach, with a very grievous blow.

question: What do the people ask of Judah and Zion?
choices: Whether the Lord has utterly rejected and loathed them
Whether the Lord is in the land
explanation: Hast thou utterly rejected Judah? hath thy soul lothed Zion? why hast thou smitten us, and there is no healing for us?

question: What title does Jeremiah give the Lord when he prays?
choices: The hope of Israel, its saviour in time of trouble
explanation: O the hope of Israel, the saviour thereof in time of trouble, why shouldest thou be as a stranger in the land?

question: What did the wild asses snuff up like dragons?
explanation: The wild asses did stand in the high places, they snuffed up the wind like dragons; their eyes did fail, because there was no grass.

question: What did the nobles’ little ones bring back from the pits?
explanation: They came to the pits, and found no water; they returned with their vessels empty.

question: What should Jeremiah’s eyes do night and day?
explanation: Let mine eyes run down with tears night and day, and let them not cease.

question: What three things will the Lord use to consume the people?
explanation: I will consume them by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence.

question: What does the Lord call the false prophets’ vision?
choices: A false vision, divination and a thing of nought
explanation: They prophesy unto you a false vision and divination, and a thing of nought, and the deceit of their heart.

question: Who does Jeremiah say go about in a land they know not?
explanation: Both the prophet and the priest go about into a land that they know not.

question: What did the people look for, and what came instead?
choices: Rain and harvest, but famine came
Peace and a time of healing, but trouble came
Victory and wealth, but defeat came
Rest and a king, but exile came
explanation: We looked for peace, and there is no good; and for the time of healing, and behold trouble!

question: What do the people not want the Lord to disgrace?
explanation: Do not abhor us, for thy name’s sake, do not disgrace the throne of thy glory.

question: What does the Lord say he will pour on the people and their families?
explanation: I will pour their wickedness upon them.

question: Why will the people wait upon the Lord?
choices: Because he has made all these things
Because there is no other land
explanation: Therefore we will wait upon thee: for thou hast made all these things.

question: What is said of the gates of Judah?
explanation: Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground.
